title: Conjecture B of Keith and Zanello on the parity of eta-powers is false
description:
This is AI-generated research: the results, proofs and code were found and written by AI. Credit goes to all the humans whose work it builds on.

Keith and Zanello (Ann. Comb. 2026, Conjecture B) conjectured that for every prime $p$ there are infinitely many odd $t$ such that, for some base $r$, the coefficients $c_t(N)$ of $f_1^t = \prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^t = \sum_{N\ge0} c_t(N)\,q^N$ are even on the $p-1$ progressions $N = p^2 n + kp + r$, $1 \le k \le p-1$. We show that at $p = 73$ exactly twenty odd $t$ have this property, the largest being $t = 203$, so the conjecture is false.

Proved in Lean 4 with Mathlib, with only the standard axioms: the falsity of Conjecture B and the result at $p = 73$ (Theorem 1 of the paper; KeithZanello.conjectureB_false, checked by Comparator). By computation: Theorems 2 and 3 of the paper ($p = 97$, and the thirty primes $p \equiv 1 \pmod{24}$ below 2000), by certificates that the repository reruns, partly redone by a second program.
